pages.x: For nearly three centuries Christians were a small, often distrusted faith in the empire, persecuted now and then. In 303 the emperor Diocletian ordered churches pulled down, scriptures burned and Christians forced to sacrifice to the gods. Thousands were killed.

In 312 Constantine, one of several rivals for the throne, marched on Rome. Before the battle at the Milvian Bridge, Christian writers later said, he saw a cross of light in the sky with the words: in this sign, conquer. His soldiers painted a Christian sign on their shields, and he won.

In 313 Constantine and his fellow emperor Licinius agreed at Milan that everyone, Christians too, could worship as they chose, and that church property should be given back. Constantine built great churches in Rome and Jerusalem and gave bishops wealth and power.

Christians quarrelled over whether Jesus was fully equal to God the Father. In 325 Constantine called some 300 bishops to Nicaea, the first council of the whole Church. They agreed the Nicene Creed, which most churches still say today.
In 330 Constantine moved his capital east, to the old Greek town of Byzantium on the Bosporus, rebuilt as Constantinople.
pages.fx: It was the capital of the eastern Roman Empire for over a thousand years, and is now Istanbul.

pages.x: Constantine put off being baptised until he lay dying in 337, as many did then, so that all his sins would be washed away at once. In 361 his nephew Julian, who loved the old gods, became emperor and tried to bring them back. He died fighting in Persia less than two years later.

In 380 the emperor Theodosius declared the Nicene faith the religion of all Romans, and in the 390s he banned sacrifices to the old gods and closed their temples. The Olympic Games, held in honour of Zeus, came to an end at about this time.

Within a century Christianity went from a persecuted faith to the religion of the Roman state. Through Rome it spread across Europe and far beyond, and the creeds, churches and calendar of that age still shape the lives of more than two billion Christians.
